data.head: ## The bundle read (2.1.325, static, no start) — the carry `cry-idxm4ycw`'s two items

body: - **The literal's source.** The dialog's own labels, at one site: `confirmLabel:"Yes, use my browser",cancelLabel:"No, keep browser tools off"`, `focus:"cancel"`, `cancelFirst:!0`, under `title:"Claude in Chrome extension detected"`. The rig's kept first screens B, C, D and F show the same rows: the title on row 3, `❯ No, keep browser tools off` on row 12, `Yes, use my browser` on row 13, and `Enter to confirm · Esc to keep browser tools off` on row 15. D differs only in its mode sentence. Counts: `No, keep browser tools off` stands twice in the bundle and `Claude in Chrome extension detected` twice (substring count over the file).

- **Which earlier step writes the detection cache — READ STATICALLY:** the cache `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` is written by `SD` (the background `aK` scan, writing `true` on a detected extension) and by three install or setup flows that verify never runs. `SD` is reached through `MIs` alone: the chrome `MIs` has 3 substring hits, its definition, an unrelated `isAbsolute as MIs` alias and one call, at the start's setup `Ud=!co&&!lo&&!Js&&MIs(v)`. In `MIs`, `lTo()&&(SD(e)||dTo())` runs `SD` only when `lTo()` holds, and `lTo` requires `Ul()`, which is `launchOptions.isInteractive()`. So the **print-mode probe cannot run the scan**, and **Run A, the first interactive start, is the one earlier step that can write the cache**. The first interactive start reads the cache as `false` (`SD` returns the cached value while its scan runs), so it raises no prompt, which matches S0C. **Still unmeasured, live only:** whether Run A's scan finishes and writes the cache before Run A is killed at its trust dialog, after 459–741 ms (the scan's own bound is not traced). A start that records the cache's value around Run A can show it.

   - a stamp of the 23 pre-chunk ids, every one `pass`, reads `cli_verified:false`;
   - the 24 ids with `browser-tools-prompt` `absent` read `cli_verified:true`;
   - the same with `fail` read `cli_verified:false`.

title: C. The gate's refusal, nothing sent

data.head: ### C. The gate's refusal, nothing sent

body:
9. **The gate** — `src/run/gate.rs`: no code change. Unit case `verdict_refuses_at_once_on_the_browser_tools_prompt`,
   built with `Some(&SIGNATURES)` as the file's `:508` cases are: a screen holding the browser-tools rows beside the
   box's own rows reads `Done(InputNotReady)` on its FIRST verdict, with the clock not advanced. With
   `sigs` `None` the same screen is `Ready`, which is the partial gate on an unverified CLI (architecture ·
   `decision/partial-gate-on-unverified-cli`): one more case pins that, unchanged.

10. **Nothing sent** — `tests/cli_send.rs`: `send_on_a_verified_cli_refuses_while_the_browser_tools_prompt_is_up`,
    modelled on `send_on_a_verified_cli_refuses_while_the_trust_dialog_is_up`, `:1199`.
    - Setup: a `stamped_home`; a trusted boot of the wrapper over a fixtures root that is a copy of the recorded set
      with one test-written `Screen.browser-tools.json` added (testing.md §Test data, the copy rule; the rows synthetic,
      written in the test as literals, the confirm row `  Yes, use my browser`, the selected row
      `❯ No, keep browser tools off`, and the box's own rule and prompt rows under them); the fake told
      `--start-screen browser-tools` (step 11).
    - Asserts: `viola send --json` exits 13 with exactly `{"v":1,"refusal":"not-delivered","detail":"input-not-ready"}`;
      no `send-issued` event and one `send-refused` event carrying that pair; the fake's receipt holds no `prompt` line
      and no `key` line, so NOTHING was sent (directive item 8). The case waits on records only, under the shared 12 s
      `WITHIN` (architecture S3).

11. **The start screen** — `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`: a new argv option `--start-screen <phase>` (argv only, no
    env; test-plan · `contract/fake-agent-cli/argv-only-options`; security standing S2). On an interactive start
    whose cwd is trusted (`Opts::trusted`), the fake draws the set's `Screen.<phase>.json` rows (`Opts::screen`) in
    place of the screen that start would otherwise settle on, and keeps them standing until it is killed. It answers
    nothing in it and never moves past it on its own. Every byte it reads while the screen stands is receipted as a
    `key` line, as today. Its hooks fire as on a plain trusted start (SessionStart at the start), so a booted
    wrapper's readiness is unchanged. An untrusted start (Run A) still draws the trust dialog first. A screen absent
    or unparsed draws nothing, as `--tag-turn-screen` does. No committed fixture is added: every test writes its own
    synthetic `Screen.browser-tools.json` into a test-owned fixtures root (tests standing S4). Add the option to the
    module doc's option list. A change to the fake's screens puts `cli_verify` in the gate block (it is,
    `## Test Commands`).

12. **The count sweep** — every site research §Sweeps lists (pattern `; 23]|twenty-three|23 rows|23/23`, `command grep
    -rln` over `*.rs`, 11 files, 9 changed, 2 no-change named there):
    - `tests/cli_verify.rs`: `STEPS_PASS` and `ROW_IDS` to `[&str; 24]`, the new last line
      `[24/24] browser-tools-prompt an interactive start's browser-tools prompt reads as a modal, nothing typed  absent`
      on the fake with no start screen; `STAMPED_PASS` `stamped 2.1.0  24 pass  0 fail`; every per-case summary
      literal there and in `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs` / `stamps.rs` re-derived from the first run's output, never typed
      from this plan (testing.md 2026-10-16);
    - `tests/contract_ledger_probes.rs`: `ROW_IDS` at 24, its `stamped {version}  24 pass  0 fail`;
    - `tests/support/home.rs`: the stamped home's relied rows at 24;
    - `crates/viola-e2e/src/harness/run.rs`: `LEDGER_ROWS` at 24, the `--local-live` id list naming
      `browser-tools-prompt` (architecture history: a new row updates every listed id site, not only the count);
    - `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`: the V arm's `23/23` → `24/24`.

    A sweep for stale count literals matches the retired shapes (`/23]`, `[&str; 23]`, `23 pass  0 fail`), never a bare
    `N pass` (testing.md 2026-10-14). `src/run/wheel.rs:527` and `tests/contract_fixture_hygiene.rs:735` stay.

13. **The verify browser-tools case** — `tests/cli_verify/runs.rs`:
    `verify_reads_the_browser_tools_prompt_as_a_modal_and_pastes_nothing`, modelled on
    `verify_pastes_no_local_command_once_the_tag_turn_screen_shows_a_modal`, `:460`.
    - Setup: `write_spine_set`, a test-written `Screen.browser-tools.json` (step 10's rows), and the fake handed
      `--receipt` and `--start-screen browser-tools`.
    - Asserts, from the stamp: `rows["browser-tools-prompt"] == "pass"`; `measured.first_screen` reads `trust` at `a`
      and `browser-tools` at every trusted run that started; `rows["modal-signature"] == "pass"` (Run A's trust
      dialog).
    - Asserts, from the receipt: `trusted_run_typed(&receipt)` is empty, nothing pasted into the prompt.
    - Asserts, from the output: the exit is 1 and the summary is copied from the first run.
    - The runs settle at once on the literal, so the case runs under the default 20 s `ci` kill, with no
      `verify_window_` prefix.

title: F. The standing rig: two arms, a no-key stop, `cache-a`, the 24th row's line

data.head: ### F. The standing rig: two arms, a no-key stop, `cache-a`, the 24th row's line

body:
14. **Two arms** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`:
    - `Arm::VP` (parse word `vp`): the verify arm with the browser-tools key NOT seeded, where the prompt must stand.
    - `Arm::VK` (parse word `vk`): the verify arm with the S0B seed, the key seeded `false`, its control.
    - Both behave as `Arm::V` everywhere `V` is matched (`has_vhome`, `verify_seed`, `marker_seed`, `trusted`, the
      `viola-build` and `--record` / `--record-first-screens` child args, `arm_v`, `kept` / `record-left`, the exit
      words), and both end through `stop_no_key`: in `run_child`, `no_key` holds `VP` and `VK`.
    - `Arm::V`'s Ctrl-C stop is not changed (`inputs#I3` item 5).
    - `of_label`: `BP` and `BP-2` → `VP`, `BK` → `VK`, and no other label. The doc comment lists them.
    - The rig types no key on either arm: `keys: none` (arm_v already prints it).

15. **The seed** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs`: `seed_used_markers` takes whether the browser-tools key is
    seeded. `VP` writes the four kept markers and leaves `claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled` out. `V`, `VK`, `VC`, `TS`
    and `TC` keep all five as today. `seed_markers_word` reads `written` for `VP` only when the four markers stand at
    their values AND the browser-tools key is absent; for every other arm it is unchanged. Nothing is read from the
    user's config (security · `decision/live-rig-seed-from-bundle-logic`). Unit case:
    `seed_used_markers_leaves_the_browser_tools_key_out_for_vp`, beside
    `seed_used_markers_writes_the_bundle_markers_and_keeps_the_seed`.

16. **`cache-a`** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` and `mod.rs`: a `Scratch` reader of the private config
    that answers `written` when the key NAME `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled` stands in it and `absent` when it does
    not. The reader reads presence only, never a value (`inputs#I3` item 5). It is read for `VP` and `VK` after
    verify has exited and before the teardown removes the scratch, and printed as `cache-a: <word>` (`unread` when the
    config cannot be read).
    - Leaned per `inputs#I3` item 5 and research §The bundle read: the rig cannot pause verify between its runs, so
      the word reads the config at verify's end. With `screen-b`'s word it says whether Run A's scan armed the prompt
      for the later runs. The plan names it so, never as a reading taken between Run A and Run B.
    - Unit case `cache_word_reads_the_key_name_only`: written / absent / unread, with a planted `true` and a planted
      `false` both reading `written`.

17. **The 24th row's line and the counts** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` `stamp_lines`:
    - one more line, `browser-tools-prompt: <word>`, the stamped word when it is a code word, else `absent` for an
      entry without it, `unread` with no entry;
    - `pass-count` and `failing` read each row through `viola_agent_claude::ledger::counts` (by `LedgerRow::ALL`'s
      ids; an id outside them reads by `== "pass"`), so `BK`'s `absent` is counted in `24/24` and is not failing;
    - `FLOOR_ROWS` stays the 21 ids (decisive: `BK`'s `failing: none` reads all 24, and `BP` asserts no floor).

    The rig's own unit cases for `stamp_lines` take a `browser-tools-prompt` row in all three words.

18. **The rehearsals** — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` (over the fake agent, run in CI; test-plan ·
    `decision/standing-live-rig`):
    - `rig_rehearsal_vp_reads_the_browser_tools_prompt_and_types_nothing`: the `vp` arm over the fake with a
      test-written `Screen.browser-tools.json` and `--start-screen browser-tools`. It asserts
      `browser-tools-prompt: pass`, `seed-markers: written`, `keys: none`, a `stop:` line that is not `ctrl-c`,
      `cache-a: absent` (the fake writes no cache), and the teardown words.
    - `rig_rehearsal_vk_reads_24_rows_with_the_browser_tools_row_absent`: the `vk` arm over the fake with no start
      screen. It asserts `rows: 24`, `pass-count: 24/24`, `failing: none`, `browser-tools-prompt: absent` and
      `keys: none`.
    - The `V` arm's rehearsal moves to `24/24`. Every rehearsal case is tied and bounded as the file's existing ones.

19. **The live starts' ledger and the founder's real config** — no code change. `BP` and `BK` write one fresh ledger,
    `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-18-browser-tools-prompt-modal/evidence/prompt-starts.ndjson`. Each start's line
    is written with the clock's time before the spawn, by the rig's ledger admission. A start refused for the token
    window writes no line and is uncounted: implement stops and says so, and sets no timer. The founder's real
    `~/.claude.json` is read only by the rig's mark witness (`user-config`); nothing of it is copied but key NAMES
    (security · `decision/live-rig-isolated-child`, `decision/live-rig-credentials-copy`).
20. **Gates first**: entries 1–7 green (`## Test Commands`), the controls held, before the round.

21. **The round** (`gate.py run --chunk 2026-11-18-browser-tools-prompt-modal --run-dir {implement run dir}
    --live-legs`, backgrounded): entries 8–14 in block order. `BP` fires first (`--cap 1 --spare 1`), then `BK`
    (`--cap 2 --spare 1`). `--cap` counts the base starts in the ledger FILE, whatever their label: `BP` is the first
    base line and `BK` the second, so each entry's `--cap` is the running total at that entry. The spare `BP-2` is a
    `-2` label, counted by `--spare`. The round stops at the first entry that is not green (gate-contract §Live round),
    so a RED `BP` leaves `BK` unfired.

22. **A RED live entry stops implement before the operator pass** (`inputs#I3` item 7). Implement records the summary
    whole in `evidence/live-starts.md` and names the cause from the summary's own words: the `screen-*` words,
    `browser-tools-prompt:`, `cache-a:`, `verify-exit:` and the teardown words. If `BP` reads `box` throughout, its
    record names `cache-a` and the screens. The spare `BP-2` is spent only on a cause `BP` ITSELF showed (a kept frame,
    a closed word), after its mend lands through a plan revision, never on an inference. The research's example mend:
    `box` throughout with `cache-a: absent`, mended by seeding the CLI's own `cachedChromeExtensionInstalled: true`,
    the value the CLI writes itself. A third base start is the founder's. No key is added for any reading.

23. **Resuming at one entry**: `--entry {n}` fires the round steps since the previous live leg, then the leg.
    - Resuming at `BP` (entry 11) fires entries 8–10, then 11.
    - Resuming at `BK` (entry 13) fires entry 12, the census after `BP`, then 13.
    - The census after `BK` (entry 14) is the round's last step, fired only by the whole round. A resume at `BK` alone
      records, as its after-census, `BK`'s own `census: 0` atom and the round tool's termination census line, and
      says so in `evidence/live-starts.md`.
24. **The operator pass** (operator entries 15–21) runs only on a round reading `round: COMPLETE · legs fired 2/2`.

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs` — the three named modal literals and the untrusted-start slice, `FirstScreen::BrowserTools`, `first_screen` by constant, unit cases

- `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs` — `LedgerRow::BrowserToolsPrompt` (24th, `ALL: [Self; 24]`), its reading, `row_word` public with the new arm, `counts`, `verified` through it, `modal-signature` and `trust-record`'s Run A on the untrusted slice

- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs` — `VP`'s seed without the browser-tools key, `seed_markers_word`, the `cache-a` reader
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs` — the `FirstScreen` match arm, if the compiler names one
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the `vp` and `vk` rehearsals, the `V` arm at 24/24
The block runs, in order:
- the formatter and the linter;
- the agent crate's unit suite (the literal, the word, the row's three readings, `counts`, `verified`);

- the root bin's unit layer (verify's lines and settle, the gate's refusal at once, the rig's arms, seed, `cache-a`
  and stamp lines, which are viola-e2e inline cases);
- the whole integration and E2E layers: every stamped binary and the harness boot stamp 24 rows;
- the live round of `BP` and `BK` (step 21).
What is not run, and why:

- The release check: the new option lives in the test-only `viola-fake-agent` binary (`required-features =
  ["fake-agent"]`) and the rig in the test-only `viola-e2e`, both already refused by `scripts/release-check.sh`. No
  product code reads either (security standing S2).
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 8; testing.md 2026-10-04).
Waits and kills:
- Every root test that waits keeps the shared 12 s `WITHIN` under the 20 s lint.

- The verify-driven cases have no test-side bound: the `ci` 20 s kill is theirs (test-plan
  `decision/verify-driven-tests-20s-kill`), and the `verify_window_` class keeps its 80 s.
- No new settle is waited out: the browser-tools screen settles at once.
Test homes: every test start runs under a test-owned user home (testing.md 2026-11-18).

The operator pass: verify's output feeds the harness boot (`LEDGER_ROWS`), so the pass boots one session
`screen-smoke`, reads its status and cleans it up (boot never piped).

The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it: the install read by path, the rig's census and
the build's hash. None of them primes anything. The round's census after each leg is set out in step 23, for the
whole round and for a resume at one entry.

The remove-the-guard controls are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, not entries (validation.md check 4
(6)). Each is fired with the `--timeout` named below, on an entry whose build reaches every binary its case needs.
«holds» means the named case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line; a `timeout` reading is not «holds». Each id is at
most 16 characters, and each case is named as nextest prints the NAME (testing.md 2026-11-14), copied from the first
run.

- `bt-literal` — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/screen.rs`: the browser-tools literal removed from
  `SIGNATURES.modals`; case `verdict_refuses_at_once_on_the_browser_tools_prompt`, fired on entry 4 (`run --unit`, a
  workspace-building layer; testing.md 2026-11-13) with `--timeout 900`. With the guard gone the first verdict is a
  wait, not `Done(InputNotReady)`. This is measured at implement.

- `bt-absent` — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`: the `absent` clause of `counts` removed; case
  `verified_reads_the_browser_tools_row_absent_as_counting`, fired on entry 3 with `--timeout 600`. With the guard
  gone the stamp reads unverified. This is measured at implement.

- `bt-none` — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`: the "none reads `none`" clause removed from the row's
  reading; case `browser_tools_row_reads_fail_when_a_first_screen_reads_none`, fired on entry 3 with `--timeout 600`.
  With the guard gone the row reads `absent`. This is measured at implement.

- `bt-modalsig` — `crates/viola-agent-claude/src/ledger.rs`: `ModalSignature` reading the whole modal set again; case
  `modal_signature_fails_on_a_browser_tools_screen_at_run_a`, fired on entry 3 with `--timeout 600`. With the guard
  gone the row passes. This is measured at implement.
